questions.question: What would happen to a commercial bank if all of its depositors arrive on the exact same morning demanding to withdraw their entire savings in cash?
options: The bank would immediately double its profits by collecting withdrawal fees
The bank would print new paper currency in its back office within ten minutes
The bank would face a liquidity crisis ('bank run') and be unable to pay all depositors immediately because most funds are tied up in long-term loans
The bank manager would be declared the permanent governor of the Reserve Bank
questions.explanation: Banks keep only a small proportion of deposits as cash and use a major portion to extend loans. If all depositors demanded their entire balances at the same time, the bank could be unable to meet all withdrawals immediately because much of the deposited money has been lent out. This is a liquidity problem; it does not by itself establish that the bank is insolvent.

questions.question: How does a bank-to-bank digital payment such as UPI or NEFT relate to demand deposits?
options: They instruct the banking system to transfer funds from the payer’s bank account to the recipient’s bank account without using paper currency
They create new currency notes issued by private payment companies
They are unrelated to bank accounts and always settle through physical cash
They convert every bank deposit into a fixed deposit automatically
questions.explanation: UPI and NEFT allow electronic payments from one bank account to another without using paper currency. They are payment mechanisms, not themselves demand deposits or currency notes. The exact processing and settlement details depend on the payment system.

questions.question: Why can it be difficult for authorities to supervise the lending activities of informal credit providers?
options: Informal lenders include varied persons such as moneylenders, traders, employers, relatives and friends, and there is no organisation supervising their credit activities in the way the RBI supervises formal lenders
Informal lenders are all registered with and directly supervised by the RBI
All informal loans are issued through the stock exchange
The Constitution prohibits any regulation of private lending
questions.explanation: NCERT lists moneylenders, traders, employers, relatives and friends among informal lenders and explains that no organisation supervises their credit activities in the same way the RBI supervises formal sources. The variety and dispersed nature of these arrangements make supervision more difficult; the question does not assume that every loan is undocumented.

questions.question: What approach to credit did Professor Muhammad Yunus and Grameen Bank help demonstrate?
options: Small loans and group-based lending can help people with limited assets access credit, although outcomes depend on the terms of lending and borrowers’ circumstances
Only wealthy households can repay small loans
Microcredit guarantees that every borrower will escape poverty
Group lending removes all financial and repayment risks
questions.explanation: Grameen Bank became known for extending small loans to poor borrowers, particularly women, through group-based lending arrangements. The model illustrated one way to widen access to credit for people who may lack conventional collateral; it does not mean that microcredit guarantees poverty reduction or eliminates repayment risk.

questions.subtopic: Summary: The Dual Nature of Credit
questions.question: Which statement accurately summarizes the dual potential of credit in an economy?
options: Credit can either be a vital catalyst for income growth and enterprise or a devastating mechanism that pushes vulnerable borrowers into severe debt-traps
Credit always leads to bankruptcy and ruin for all borrowers
Credit guarantees that every borrower becomes an industrial billionaire
Credit is economically meaningless in modern market systems
questions.explanation: Whether credit will be beneficial or harmful depends on the risks in the situation (crop failure vs assured contract) and whether there is some support, fair interest, and collateral security for the borrower.
